# Windows Cursor Simulation: full reference

Canonical URL: https://realsilasyang.github.io/windows-cursor-simulation/
Source: https://github.com/realSilasYang/windows-cursor-simulation
Specification: CSS Basic User Interface Module Level 4, https://www.w3.org/TR/css-ui-4/#cursor
Last updated: 2026-08-09

## Purpose and observable behavior

Windows Cursor Simulation is a free, static web application for inspecting the pointer produced by CSS `cursor` values. Each test card applies a standard CSS keyword to its own interactive area. The visible pointer therefore comes from the visitor's current browser, operating system, and configured system pointer scheme.

The site does not fetch or apply cursor image resources. In particular, it does not reference `.cur` or `.ani` files from the author's local cursor collection. Results can differ across browsers, operating systems, themes, display scaling settings, and accessibility configurations.

## Counts

- Total predefined CSS cursor keywords tested: 36
- Keywords mapped to standard Windows cursor-scheme roles: 13
- CSS states without a dedicated standard Windows cursor-scheme role: 23
- Interface languages: 14, plus an automatic browser-language mode
- Use-case groups: 5

## Windows role mapping

| CSS keyword | Windows cursor-scheme role | Classification |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `auto` | none; browser chooses | CSS state |
| `default` | `Arrow` | Windows system role |
| `none` | none; pointer hidden | CSS state |
| `context-menu` | no dedicated standard slot | CSS state |
| `help` | `Help` | Windows system role |
| `progress` | `AppStarting` | Windows system role |
| `wait` | `Wait` | Windows system role |
| `not-allowed` | `No` | Windows system role |
| `no-drop` | no dedicated standard slot | CSS state |
| `pointer` | `Hand` | Windows system role |
| `text` | `IBeam` | Windows system role |
| `vertical-text` | no dedicated standard slot | CSS state |
| `crosshair` | `Crosshair` | Windows system role |
| `cell` | no dedicated standard slot | CSS state |
| `move` | `SizeAll` | Windows system role |
| `grab` | no dedicated standard slot | CSS state |
| `grabbing` | no dedicated standard slot | CSS state |
| `alias` | no dedicated standard slot | CSS state |
| `copy` | no dedicated standard slot | CSS state |
| `all-scroll` | no dedicated standard slot | CSS state |
| `col-resize` | no dedicated standard slot | CSS state |
| `row-resize` | no dedicated standard slot | CSS state |
| `n-resize` | no dedicated standard slot | CSS state |
| `e-resize` | no dedicated standard slot | CSS state |
| `s-resize` | no dedicated standard slot | CSS state |
| `w-resize` | no dedicated standard slot | CSS state |
| `ne-resize` | no dedicated standard slot | CSS state |
| `nw-resize` | no dedicated standard slot | CSS state |
| `se-resize` | no dedicated standard slot | CSS state |
| `sw-resize` | no dedicated standard slot | CSS state |
| `ns-resize` | `SizeNS` | Windows system role |
| `ew-resize` | `SizeWE` | Windows system role |
| `nwse-resize` | `SizeNWSE` | Windows system role |
| `nesw-resize` | `SizeNESW` | Windows system role |
| `zoom-in` | no dedicated standard slot | CSS state |
| `zoom-out` | no dedicated standard slot | CSS state |

The phrases “CSS state” and “no dedicated standard slot” mean that Windows does not expose a separate cursor-scheme entry for that exact CSS semantic role. They do not guarantee identical artwork across browsers or platforms.

## Use-case groups

1. General actions: `auto`, `default`, `none`, `context-menu`, `help`, `progress`, `wait`, `not-allowed`, `no-drop`, `pointer`.
2. Text and precision selection: `text`, `vertical-text`, `crosshair`, `cell`.
3. Movement and drag-and-drop: `move`, `grab`, `grabbing`, `alias`, `copy`, `all-scroll`.
4. Resizing: `col-resize`, `row-resize`, `n-resize`, `e-resize`, `s-resize`, `w-resize`, `ne-resize`, `nw-resize`, `se-resize`, `sw-resize`, `ns-resize`, `ew-resize`, `nwse-resize`, `nesw-resize`.
5. View zoom: `zoom-in`, `zoom-out`.
